source: Master Knowledge v3 (data/food-policy/master-knowledge.v3.md), sections 4 to 8 and 20, plus the everyday food list in data/food-policy/everyday-foods.v1.json. Owner-written logic; additions by Maya are marked there for owner review.

verdicts.JA: Everyday choice in normal amounts (shown as Everyday / Alltag / Diario)
verdicts.SELTEN: Small portion: keep to the portion, best with a meal (shown as Small portion / Kleine Portion / Porción pequeña; no frequency)
verdicts.NEIN: Skip it: pick a swap instead (shown as Skip it / Lieber nicht / Mejor no)

combine: The strictest verdict of all matching rules wins; ties are named by the earliest stage in priority. JA only comes from a JA rule. Nothing (protein, fibre, fat, a claim or a score) can lift a safety, medical or policy NEIN. Without a JA rule a product is at best SELTEN.

rules.when: one of the user's allergens is in the ingredients
rules.why: Contains {0}, which is on your allergy list

rules.when: the user has allergies and the ingredients are missing or unreadable
rules.why: Ingredients missing, so your allergens cannot be ruled out

rules.when: a category on the user's medical/avoid list matches
rules.why: On your avoid list ({0})

rules.when: pork: category, name or ingredient
rules.why: Pork product

rules.when: alcohol: category, name or ingredient
rules.why: Alcoholic drink or alcohol inside

rules.when: a drink with added sugar or at least sugarDrinkPer100ml sugar per 100 ml, or a soft drink category (smoothies have their own rule, policy.smoothie)
rules.why: Sugary drink: liquid sugar hits fast

rules.when: fruit juice, nectar or juice spritzer
rules.why: Juice is liquid sugar, even without added sugar

rules.when: a fruit smoothie. Master Knowledge v3 lists typical smoothies as NEIN; since Oct 25 2026 they get their own reason so a smoothie is not called a soda (blending leaves less intact fibre than whole fruit; NHS counts smoothie sugar as free sugar). Added sugar or a soft-drink category still adds policy.sugar_drink
rules.why: Smoothie: blended fruit, less fibre than whole fruit

rules.when: a drink sweetened with sweeteners (Zero/light soft drinks) as a habitual replacement
rules.why: Sweetened 'zero' drink: keeps the sweet habit going

rules.when: candy, chocolate, biscuits, cakes, ice cream, puddings and other conventional sweet desserts (sweetened high-protein desserts included)
rules.why: Sweets or sweet dessert

rules.when: a solid food with at least sugarHeavySolidPer100 g sugar per 100 g and added sugar (or no ingredient list to prove otherwise); fruit, plain dairy and dried-fruit-only lists excluded
rules.why: Sugar-heavy ({0} g sugar per 100 g), treated like sweets

rules.when: nuts with a sugar/honey/chocolate coating, or nuts with added sugar in the first three ingredients
rules.why: Sugar-coated nuts

rules.when: rice, bread (whole-grain too), regular pasta, potatoes, breakfast cereals
rules.why: Starchy staple: a large load of fast carbohydrate

rules.when: chips, crisps, crackers, pretzels and similar processed snacks
rules.why: Processed starchy snack

rules.when: ketchup, BBQ and other sweet sauces, syrups, jams and sweet spreads
rules.why: Sweet sauce or spread

rules.when: oats, quinoa, couscous, bulgur, millet, polenta, semolina, corn, rice cakes, flour (Master Knowledge section 7)
rules.why: Grain or starchy base: a large load of carbohydrate

rules.when: sugar or syrup itself, in any form (Master Knowledge section 7)
rules.why: Sugar or syrup: added sugar

rules.when: banana, mango, dates, grapes, pineapple, figs, dried fruit (Master Knowledge section 7)
rules.why: Very sweet fruit: a lot of sugar at once

rules.when: breaded, battered or deep-fried foods (Master Knowledge section 7)
rules.why: Breaded or fried: a crust of fast starch

rules.when: whole-grain or legume pasta
rules.why: Whole-grain pasta: still a lot of carbohydrate, keep it small

rules.when: plain nuts above defaults.portionG.nuts per serving
rules.why: Plain nuts, but a large portion ({0} g)

rules.when: cheese above defaults.portionG.cheese per serving
rules.why: Cheese, but a large portion ({0} g)

rules.when: lentils, chickpeas, beans, hummus
rules.why: Legumes: fibre and protein, but still carbohydrate

rules.when: sweet potato
rules.why: Sweet potato: only in controlled portions

rules.when: apples, pears, citrus, stone fruit, melon, berries: whole fruit in a small portion (Master Knowledge sections 6 and 20)
rules.why: Whole fruit: a small portion

rules.when: berries above a small handful (80 g) per serving (Master Knowledge section 20)
rules.why: Berries: a bowlful is more sugar than a handful

rules.when: halloumi and grilling cheese (Master Knowledge section 6)
rules.why: Halloumi: salty and rich, keep the portion small

rules.when: peanut butter, nut butters, tahini: easy to eat in large amounts (Master Knowledge section 6)
rules.why: Nut butter: one spoon fits, the jar goes fast

rules.when: processed protein products (protein isolate, protein claims); protein never makes a product green
rules.why: Processed protein product: protein does not make it a standard choice

rules.when: sausages, cold cuts, breaded meat (non-pork)
rules.why: Processed meat

rules.when: sweet-and-salty snack mixes
rules.why: Sweet and salty snack mix

rules.when: the ingredients are missing, unreadable or cut off and no NEIN rule applies (provisional yellow)
rules.why: Ingredients missing or incomplete: provisional rating

rules.when: added sugar in the first three ingredients, and more than 5 g sugar per 100 g (2.5 g per 100 ml); at or under that the EU calls it low sugar, Regulation (EC) 1924/2006
rules.why: Added sugar near the top

rules.when: a sweetener or sugar alcohol anywhere
rules.why: Has a sweetener ({0})

rules.when: refined starch in the first three ingredients
rules.why: Refined starch near the top ({0})

rules.when: marketing claims (High Protein, Low Carb, Keto, Zero, Sugar free, Organic, Gluten free) are recorded but never approve
rules.why: Claims on the pack do not change the rating

rules.when: Higher estimated blood sugar impact for the serving (24 Oct 2026: the Food check never says a higher spike estimate is fine, same as meals)
rules.why: Higher estimated blood sugar impact for this serving

rules.when: not enough data to estimate and no whole-food JA rule
rules.why: Not enough data to estimate: provisional rating

rules.when: eggs
rules.why: Eggs

rules.when: unbreaded chicken or turkey
rules.why: Chicken or turkey

rules.when: lean beef
rules.why: Lean beef

rules.when: fresh fish
rules.why: Fish

rules.when: non-starchy vegetables
rules.why: Non-starchy vegetables

rules.when: water, tea or coffee with no sugar and no sweetener
rules.why: Unsweetened drink

rules.when: olive oil, avocado
rules.why: Whole-food fat in normal amounts

rules.when: plain tofu or tempeh
rules.why: Tofu or tempeh: plant protein

rules.when: cream cheese, cottage cheese, ricotta without added sugar (Master Knowledge section 5)
rules.why: Fresh cheese without sugar

rules.when: plain berries, a small handful (80 g or less) per serving
rules.why: Berries in a small handful

rules.when: milk to drink: more than a splash (about 50 ml) per serving, or plain milk with no coffee or tea around it (Master Knowledge v3, the milk portion rule)
rules.why: Milk by the glass: a lot of milk sugar as a liquid

rules.when: milk as a splash (about 50 ml or less) in coffee or tea, no sugar added; plant drinks are rated by their own rules
rules.why: A splash of milk without added sugar

rules.when: plain nuts (ingredient list known, no added sugar, no coating) up to defaults.portionG.nuts per serving
rules.why: Plain nuts in a moderate portion

rules.when: cheese up to defaults.portionG.cheese per serving, no added sugar
rules.why: Cheese in a moderate portion
